notes: Summary: Financial trading platform evaluating Redwood Dedicated / Private for low-latency inference (decisioning + chat ops). Priority = deterministic p95/p99 under peak load; streaming behavior must be aligned with product UX.

Workload profile: mixture of streaming chat (ticketing and human-in-the-loop alerts) and synchronous scoring for trading signals. ~35% streaming, 65% non-streaming. Average request size: 800 tokens for scoring, 1.5k tokens for some analyst chat flows.

Targets proposed by customer (initial): non-streaming: p50 <= 30ms, p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 300ms; streaming first-byte (server-to-client) p50 <= 15ms, p95 <= 80ms, p99 <= 250ms. Wants p95 guarantee for tail latency credits in SLA.

Measurement ambiguity: customer currently measures end-to-end from client (mobile/web) including client processing and WAN. Redwood measures at gateway + runtime. Need alignment: agree to publish both server-side and RUM-style client metrics and a mapping for peering/last-mile delta.

Routing & fallback: must support deterministic fallback to a smaller quantized model (90% feature parity) if latency SLOs are violated. Must preserve order for streaming partial responses when falling back.

Capacity ask: design to sustain 1k sustained RPS at 1k tokens avg with 3x burst headroom to 3k RPS. Customer prefers H100-class nodes but open to A100 with multi-instance and quantized variants. Wants guidance on reserved fleet sizing and expected utilization targets.
SLA asks: specific credit schedule for p95 breaches, regional residency (EU/NA) for accounting/regulatory streams, mandatory audit logging per request (token-level audit) for compliance audits.

Instrumentation goals: agree on the following measurable events for SLOs: client-invoke (client timestamp), edge-arrival (load balancer), request-dispatch (runtime), first-token-emitted, last-token-emitted, response-delivered (edge). Correlate IDs across traces and expose sample traces in Console.

Success criteria for POC: 1) measured p95 under synthetic mixed workload <= target for two 4-hour runs, 2) pass security checklist and peering tests, 3) validated model fallback preserves stream semantics, 4) runbook for operational escalations.
Quote from CTO on call: 'We need guarantees that the tail won't blow up during market open — and we need to be able to explain the delta between what users see and what you measure.'
